source: R. H. Bow, Economics of Construction in relation to Framed Structures, London: Spon, 1873, Part I, tables of roof trusses (pp. 17-30) and framed bridges (pp. 31-40); each design redrawn as an exact construction from the printed drawing
units: nodes in spans (support to support = 1, z up); span in mm; radii (half square sections) in mm
sizing: span: Bow's where stated, else sub-spans x 8 ft; roof 1.5 kN/m2 on the roof outline, deck 5 kN/m2, trusses 3 m apart, x 1.4; truss action as in a force diagram (pin-jointed, curved chords one bar between joints, bending from loads between joints and the sagitta, members landing beside a joint meeting it with their eccentricity as bending), frames with rigid joints only where the pin-jointed frame is a mechanism (analysis); square GL24h sections, N/A + M/W within design strength, buckling of struts; one section per member
joints: chord_levels, web_levels, post_levels: the hierarchy, 1 primary, 2 secondary, 3 tertiary, a member stopping on the higher ones at its node; runs_on: chord ends (chord, 0 start or 1 end) that run on where chord ends meet
